name: Białowieża Forest
tagline: One of the last primeval lowland forests in Europe, home to the continent's largest land animal, the European bison.
highlight: Watching a European bison emerge from the mist in the forest.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed ancient forest on the Belarus border, with European bison, old oaks, guided walks, horse-drawn carts and a quiet village with wooden houses.
metaDescription: A Białowieża Forest travel guide: European bison, the strictly protected zone, guided walks, the Bison Show Reserve, wooden houses, birdwatching, how to get there, where to stay and a two-day plan.
nearestAirport: Warsaw Chopin (WAW), about 3–4 hours by road; Białystok train and bus
goodFor: Wildlife, nature lovers, birdwatchers, quiet travel

image.alt: Ancient trees in Białowieża National Park

intro: Białowieża Forest straddles the border between Poland and Belarus, and is one of the last and largest remaining parts of the primeval forest that once covered the European plain. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its oaks, hornbeams and spruces, some over 400 years old, grow among fallen logs and mossy ground that have been left to rot naturally for centuries.

The forest's flagship animal is the European bison, the wisent, the heaviest land mammal in Europe. It was hunted to extinction in the wild by 1919, and was reintroduced from zoo animals here, and today about 800 live in the forest on the Polish side. Also present are wolves, lynx, elk, red deer, and many rare birds and beetles, and the forest is a prime birdwatching site for woodpeckers and owls.

The strictly protected core of Białowieża National Park can only be visited with a licensed guide, on foot or in a horse-drawn cart, while wider areas can be explored independently. The village of Białowieża has wooden houses, guesthouses and a palace park. It is remote, about four hours from Warsaw, and the best visits are two days in late spring or autumn.

whyVisit.intro: Białowieża is a rare chance to see a real ancient forest and Europe's largest land mammal.

attractionsIntro: Most visits combine guided walks in the strict reserve with independent trails.

foodIntro: Local food is simple and eastern Polish, with Belarusian influence.

gettingThere.intro: Białowieża is remote, and usually reached via Białystok or Hajnówka.

options.text: From Warsaw, about 4 to 5 hours in total.

gettingAround.intro: The village is small, and trails start nearby.

bestTime.headline: May–June and September–October
bestTime.summary: The forest is lovely in spring and autumn, and bison are active at dawn.

seasons.text: Snowy, with bison easier to see.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you plan.

faq.a: Often but not always. The Show Reserve is a sure option.
Train or bus via Hajnówka, or drive.

faq.q: Is it safe near the border?
faq.a: Yes, but check current advice, since the Belarus border area has restrictions.
